content.title: What are Serialization and Deserialization?
content.description: Serialization is the process of converting a Java object into a byte stream for storage or transmission. Deserialization is the reverse process of reconstructing the object from the byte stream.

content.content: In Java, objects exist only while a program is running. To save an object's state permanently or send it over a network, it must first be converted into a stream of bytes. This process is called Serialization. Later, the byte stream can be converted back into the original object through Deserialization.

content.title: Why Learn Serialization?
content.content: Serialization is widely used in file storage, distributed systems, caching, networking, session management, and remote communication.
Serialization
Serialization converts an object's current state into a sequence of bytes that can be stored in a file or transmitted across a network.

content.title: Serializable Class
Important Requirement
content.description: A class must implement the Serializable interface to allow its objects to be serialized.

Deserialization reconstructs an object from its serialized byte stream using ObjectInputStream.

content.title: Deserialization Example
Key Benefit
content.content: Serialization preserves the state of an object, allowing it to be restored later exactly as it was.
Serializable Interface
Serializable is a marker interface that contains no methods. Its purpose is simply to indicate that objects of a class can be serialized.
The transient Keyword
The transient keyword prevents specific fields from being serialized. Such fields are skipped during serialization and receive default values during deserialization.

content.content: Real-Life Analogy

content.title: Packing and Unpacking a Parcel
content.content: Serialization is like packing your belongings into a sealed parcel so they can be transported safely. Deserialization is unpacking the parcel to retrieve the original items exactly as they were.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Serialization is a common Java interview topic. Questions often cover Serializable, transient, ObjectOutputStream, ObjectInputStream, serialVersionUID, and object persistence.
Common Mistakes

items.question: What happens if Serializable is not implemented?
items.answer: Java throws a NotSerializableException during serialization.

items.question: Can transient variables be serialized?
items.answer: No. They are skipped during serialization.

items.question: Should streams always be closed?
items.answer: Yes. Closing streams releases system resources and ensures proper file handling.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: Serialization converts objects into byte streams, while deserialization restores those byte streams back into Java objects.
